fieldMarks: Adult: black face contrasting with a rich brown back, grey chest and a yellow bill.
Juvenile: lacks the black face and is buffier below; sometimes mistaken for the rare yellow rail.
behavior: Heard far more than seen: a musical series of piping notes rapidly descending the scale, and a rising 'ker-wee'.
Large numbers may gather in marshes in late summer and early fall to fatten before migrating; migrates mostly at night, many to South America.
Picks food from the surface; eats many seeds of marsh plants (heavily on wild rice in late summer and fall), plus insects and snails.
habitat: Freshwater marshes with large stands of cattails, wet meadows and grassy pond edges; also salt marshes, especially in winter.
range: Breeds across much of Canada and the northern and western United States and winters in the southern United States and south to South America; recorded in every region from Alaska and the North to Florida.

lookalikes.name: Virginia rail
lookalikes.howToTell: The Virginia rail has a long bill and rusty-cinnamon underparts; the sora is short-billed with a yellow bill and black face.

lookalikes.name: Yellow rail
lookalikes.howToTell: A juvenile sora lacks the black face and can suggest a yellow rail; check carefully.
